newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. team in Iraq to oversee hunt for missile parts.
newsitem.headline: U.N. team in Iraq to oversee hunt for missile parts.

text.p: United Nations inspectors have arrived to supervise further Iraqi excavations for missing missile parts, a U.N. official said on Friday.

"A small team of ballistic missile experts has arrived in order to support the Iraqi excavations for banned missile materials," Goran Wallen, director of Baghdad's Ongoing Monitoring and Verification Centre, told Reuters.

Last month Iraqi excavations near Baghdad uncovered four wrecked rocket engines and other components. Wallen said the fresh team would oversee Iraqi digs at other sites where they say they had destroyed and buried scores of banned long-range missiles in 1992.
The excavations are part of an Iraqi initiative to try to substantiate claims that all its banned missiles were destroyed.

A U.N. ballistic missile team under Frenchman Michael Bordin was in Baghdad from January 5 to 23 examining material uncovered by the Iraqis. The United Nations has expressed doubts about the authenticity of buried parts and suggested Iraq is still hiding missiles.
Under terms ending the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait, Iraq must rid itself of weapons of mass destruction, including missiles with ranges greater than 150 km (93 miles).
The United Nations Special Commission overseeing destruction of the banned weapons last year dug up than 100 missile parts from several sites for analysis abroad.

But UNSCOM and Baghdad are at loggerheads over how and where to analyse the parts. UNSCOM's chairman Rolf Ekeus is expected in Baghdad on February 20 for talks with Iraqi officials about the standoff.
